worked_solution:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

- For $x(t)=3\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =\frac{3}{t+1} \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =-\frac{3}{(t+1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t)=\sqrt{t},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} \\ {y}^{″}(t) & =-\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨{x}^{″}(t),\,{y}^{″}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{(t+1)^{2}},\,-\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
